title: CBSE Class 9 - SST (Economics)
subtitle: Poverty as a Challenge
description: Online practice test containing 100 high-yield objective MCQs for Class 9 Poverty as a Challenge.

questions.q: Poverty line in India is estimated on the basis of minimum level of income or:
Accepted average daily calorie requirement per person in rural areas of India is:
Accepted average daily calorie requirement per person in urban areas of India is:
Why is calorie requirement higher in rural areas than in urban areas?
o: Rural people engage in more physical labor
Food is cheaper in rural areas

questions.q: For the year 2011-12, poverty line for a person was fixed at Rs. 816 per month for rural areas and for urban areas at:
Which organization in India conducts periodic sample surveys to estimate poverty line?
World Bank uses a uniform standard for extreme poverty line, defined as living on less than (historical benchmark):
Which two social groups are most vulnerable to poverty in India?
Which economic categories are most vulnerable to poverty in India?
o: Rural agricultural labor households and Urban casual labor households

questions.q: Among the poor, who are 'poorest of the poor' because they are systematically denied equal access to resources?
o: Women, elderly people, and female infants

questions.q: Which state in India has historically maintained the highest poverty ratio alongside Bihar?
Which state reduced poverty significantly by focusing on human resource development (education and healthcare)?
Which states reduced poverty through high agricultural growth rates during Green Revolution?
Which state reduced poverty through effective public distribution of food grains (PDS)?
Which state reduced poverty significantly through land reform measures?
National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) was passed in 2005 to guarantee how many days of wage employment per year to rural households?
Under MGNREGA 2005, what fraction of proposed jobs are reserved for women?
Prime Minister Rozgar Yojana (PMRY) started in 1993 aims to create self-employment opportunities for educated unemployed youth in:
Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) launched in 1999 aims at bringing assisted poor families above poverty line by organizing them into:
Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana (PMGY) launched in 2000 provides central assistance for basic services like healthcare, primary education, rural shelter, drinking water, and:
Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) launched in December 2000 provides subsidized food grains to:
o: One crore of the poorest among BPL families
